items.title: Underscores Is First Transgender Woman Nominated for Best Dance/Electronic Recording Grammy
items.summary:
The Grammys are making history this year, with first-time nominee Underscores now the first out transgender woman to be nominated for best dance/electronic recording. The artist got the nod for “Music,” from her March album U .

Related 

Madonna & Slayyyter Lead 2027 Dance/Electronic Grammy Nominations 

Grammy Nominations 2027: See the Complete List 

Noah Kahan Reacts to 2027 Grammy Nominations Snub: 'I Was In My Feelings for a Sec' 

Many transgender women have paved the way for this accomplishment, with SOPHIE, Kim Petras, Arca, Honey Dijon, Wendy Carlos, Jackie Shane and Teddy Geiger all receiving nominations over the years. In 2023, Petras became the first transgender woman to win a Grammy, when she got the award for best pop duo/group performance for her Sam Smith collab “Unholy.”

In her acceptance speech, Petras acknowledged this achievement , saying, “I just want to thank all the incredible transgender legends before me who kicked these doors open for me so I could be here tonight. SOPHIE especially, my friend who passed away two years ago who told me this would happen and always believed in me… Madonna for fighting for LGBTQ rights. I don’t think I could be here without Madonna. My mother — I grew up next to a highway in nowhere Germany and my mother believed me that I was a girl, and I wouldn’t be here without her and her support.”

Trans women are also making history elsewhere at the 2027 Grammys, with Geese’s Emily Green being the first out trans woman nominated for best new artist, best rock performance, best alternative music performance, best alternative…
items.t: Underscores Is First Transgender Woman Nominated for Best Dance/Electronic Recording Grammy

items.title: Ella Langley Becomes First Act to Earn Top Two of TouchTunes Frontline Chart
items.summary:
For the first time since the inception of the TouchTunes Frontline and Catalog charts in 2024, the same artist occupies the top two positions of either ranking.

Ella Langley ’s “Choosin’ Texas” remains at No. 1 on the Frontline Chart for the third quarter of 2026, and Langley’s “Be Her” zooms to No. 2.

The TouchTunes charts for the third quarter of 2026 track the most played songs and artists on TouchTunes jukeboxes from July 1 to Sept. 30, 2026, with the Frontline ranking inclusive of music released in the last 18 months, followed by the Catalog tally for any music that was released more than 18 months ago. The TouchTunes Artists Chart tracks the same period, combining an artist’s plays across both rankings. TouchTunes has jukeboxes in more than 60,000 locations worldwide. Its data is not factored into other Billboard charts.

“Choosin’ Texas” has spent the entirety of 2026 at No. 1 on the Frontline Chart, after debuting at No. 2 for the fourth quarter of 2025. But while the rankings have seen similarly dominant leaders — think Shaboozey ’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy)” and, on Catalog, Chris Stapleton ’s “Tennessee Whiskey” — Q3 of 2026 marks the first time one of those acts was able to occupy the entire top two of one of the tallies, with “Be Her” up to No. 2 on Frontline after reaching No. 3 in the second quarter of the year.

In all, Langley is featured on the Frontline survey five times, four as a lead act (her Morgan Wallen duet “I Can’t Love You Anymore” at No. 11 and “Dandelion” at No. 23) and once as the featured performer on BigXthaPlug ’s “Hell at Night” at No. 6. She…
items.t: Ella Langley Becomes First Act to Earn Top Two of TouchTunes Frontline Chart

items.title: The Mavericks Band Members ‘Saddened’ by Name Rights Lawsuit From Raul Malo’s Widow
items.summary:
The remaining members of Americana band The Mavericks have responded to a lawsuit brought by the widow of their late frontman Raul Malo .

Drummer Paul Deakin, keyboardist Jerry Dale McFadden and guitarist Eddie Perez wrote in a social media statement on Wednesday (Nov. 18), “We were saddened to learn that Betty Malo filed a lawsuit against us.” Betty sued the trio last week, alleging they should be prohibited from performing as The Mavericks following her husband’s 2025 death from cancer .

Related 

Raul Malo’s Widow Sues to Stop Remaining Members of The Mavericks From Using Band Name 

CL Signs With THEBLACKLABEL, Reuniting With Longtime Producer Teddy For 'Full Circle' Moment 

Severe Weather, Radius Clauses and Finding the Next Generation of Festival Headliners: 'It's a Year-by-Year Fight to Stay Alive' 

The crux of Betty’s lawsuit is a clause in the Mavericks’ operating agreement stating that the band could only use that name so long as Raul was involved. She says the surviving members are now violating this by touring with guest singers as “The Mavericks & Friends.”

Attorneys for Deakin, McFadden and Perez claim they amended The Mavericks’ operating agreement before their current “The Music Lives On” tour to remove such restrictive language. And in Wednesday’s statement, the musicians say Betty is actually being paid handsomely for these shows.

“To clear up any speculation on this topic, we have honored the financial agreement reached with the Malo estate before the tour began, and to date, Betty has received more compensation from the tour than any individual…

items.title: El Coyote Earns Third Regional Mexican Airplay No. 1 With ‘Ranchero Enamorado’
items.summary:
El Coyote y Su Banda Tierra Santa earns its third No. 1 on Billboard ’s Regional Mexican Airplay chart as “Ranchero Enamorado” jumps 2-1 on the list dated Nov. 21. The song is the second chart-topper from the group’s album Nacimos Pa’ Ser Historia , following “ Te Dije ” in July.

Released on Andaluz/FOMO/UMLE, “Ranchero Enamorado” climbs from No. 2 with 6.9 million audience impressions earned in the United States, up 6%, during the Nov. 6-12 tracking week, according to Luminate.

Related 

El Coyote y Su Banda Tierra Santa Roars Back to No. 1 on Regional Mexican Airplay After Nearly 26 Years 

‘Pa’ Él’ Lifts Los Ángeles Azules & Tini to No. 1 on Regional Mexican Airplay Chart 

Victor Mendivil Crashes Latin Albums Chart’s Top 10 With ‘No Hay Ángeles Aquí’ 

The song switches places with Los Ángeles Azules and Tini’s “Pa’ Él,” as the latter cedes the summit, dipping 1-2, after an 11% dip in audience impressions, down to 6.4 million.

El Coyote y Su Banda Tierra Santa’s ascent to No. 1 is the fifth time this year a group has taken the top spot from a collaborative track. Banda El Recodo de Cruz de Lizárraga’s “Sólo Tú” replaced La Arrolladora Banda El Limón and Juanes’ “Una Noche Contigo” at No. 1 on the Jan. 24-dated chart. Los Dos de Tamaulipas’ “El Chavalón” then took the crown from Xavi and Carín León’s “La Morrita” on the March 7 chart. Three weeks later, Calibre 50’s “Me Enamoré Solo” pushed “La Morrita” from the lead on the March 28-dated ranking. Meanwhile, Banda Los Recoditos followed on May 23, when “En Coma Inducido” took No. 1 from Banda Los Sebastianes de Saúl…

If you weren’t old enough to catch Feist ‘s piano-pounding indie staple “My Moon, My Man” — or its block-rocking Boys Noize remix — back in 2007, chances are still pretty good you’ve been exposed to it by now. First, the song was used in a memorable opening montage sequence in the fourth episode of Canadian TV phenomenon Heated Rivalry ‘s first season in late 2025, resulting in a huge streaming bump for the song that has mostly lasted through the 2026 calendar year. Now, it’s gone doubly viral, thanks to TikTok and FINNEAS. 

The latter Grammy-nominated singer-songwriter covered the song for an Amazon Music original release back in September, in advance of Feist’s induction into the Canadian Hall of Fame. items.title: Zane Lowe Talks Interviewing Stars & Growing Apple Music Radio to 50M Unique Listeners Per Month
items.summary:
Zane Lowe has become one of the music industry’s go-to press tour stops. As global creative director at Apple Music and host of its popular Zane Lowe Show , the New Zealand-born host has become known for his conversational interview style and for being the face of the Apple Music brand.

Unlike Spotify and other competitors, Apple Music has taken an approach to editorial that’s less focused on algorithmic recommendation and playlisting and more focused on hiring radio personalities, who, like Lowe, put a face to the service’s music. While it’s now common to find artists big and small at Apple Music’s new studios in Culver City, Calif., Lowe explains that it wasn’t always this way. When he first started building the company’s voice as a destination for artist interviews, after a successful stint at BBC Radio 1, “it was kind of crickets,” he tells Billboard. 

Related 

Inside the Business of Boy Bands — From One Direction to BTS 

CL Signs With THEBLACKLABEL, Reuniting With Longtime Producer Teddy For 'Full Circle' Moment 

Severe Weather, Radius Clauses and Finding the Next Generation of Festival Headliners: 'It's a Year-by-Year Fight to Stay Alive' 

“As upsetting as that was at the time, two good things came out of it,” he says of that time 11 years ago. “Number one, it snapped me back into the reality force field of building something from scratch, and number two, it made us focus really clearly and in a big way on new and emerging artists.” Early evangelists, like a then-teenage Billie Eilish , Khalid and Bryson Tiller , quickly grew into the industry’s future stars,…

items.title: Sex Pistols’ Glen Matlock reveals work on first Faces album since 1973: “Never a dull moment”
items.summary:
Sex Pistols ’ Glen Matlock has revealed that he has worked with Faces for what will be their first album since 1973.

READ MORE: Ronnie Wood talks new Jimi Hendrix exhibition and hopes of Rolling Stones tour: “When my compadres say, ‘Let’s go’, I’ll be ready” 

The band, which features Rod Stewart , Ronnie Wood and drummer Kenney Jones, formed in 1969 from the ashes of Small Faces . In their time together, Faces recorded four studio albums, the last of which being ‘Ooh La La’, which dropped back in 1973.

They formally disbanded in 1975 after Stewart left the group, and around that time, Wood began playing with The Rolling Stones . Founding bassist Ronnie Lane passed away in 1997, and keyboardist Ian McLagan died of a stroke back in 2014 .

There has been speculation for years now that a reunion could be back on the table, and rumours gained momentum in 2020, when the three surviving members came together to perform a live rendition of ‘Stay With Me’ at that year’s BRIT Awards .

The following year, Wood spoke to The Times and said that he and his bandmates had “been recording some new Faces music”, and Stewart also teased that the trio had completed “15 tracks that are extremely worthy, some old, some new”. Jones went on to make a similar statement , saying that they had “a mixture of stuff we never released which is worthy of releasing” as well as “some new stuff which is really wonderful”.

View this post on Instagram 

Now, it looks like fans are one step closer to getting a new Faces album, as Sex Pistols’ bassist Glen Matlock shared a post online, seemingly…

items.title: NØ MAN Will Stab You In The Eye
items.summary:
The first time I heard the word "Lynchburg," or at least the first time than I can remember hearing it, I thought it was a joke. In the opening scenes from Escape From LA , John Carpenter's slightly misbegotten 1996 sequel to his classic Escape From New York , a voiceover describes a bleak future in which the US elects a hardline Christian Nationalist president, who then declares himself dictator for life and moves the US capital to his Lynchburg hometown. The film never names that president, though he's played by Cliff Robertson, the square-jawed Oscar-winning actor and future Uncle Ben. When I saw that movie in the theater, I thought everything about this president was a wild exaggeration, including his decision to relocate federal operations to this surely made-up place that's basically called Racist Murderville.

items.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ fans are pretending they’re in New Zealand to play the game early
items.summary:
Some Grand Theft Auto 6 fans have tricked their console into thinking they’re in New Zealand so they can play the game early.

READ MORE: ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ review: one of the best games ever made 

Rather than a global release, Grand Theft Auto 6 officially launches midnight November 19 local time . It means that gamers in New Zealand can return to Vice City a full 19 hours before those living in America.

Some diehards, such as streamer IShowSpeed , have actually travelled to New Zealand to play Grand Theft Auto 6 as soon as possible while others are toying with their console’s settings to bypass the geographical block.

Xbox users are going to their system settings and changing their location to New Zealand via the Language and Location menus before restarting their console.

Meanwhile PlayStation owners are having a trickier time taking a virtual visit to New Zealand. To play the game early, some users are creating a new PlayStation account based in New Zealand before buying a copy of GTA 6. They then need to enable ‘console sharing and offline play’ via their PlayStation’s ‘users and accounts’ sharing settings before they can play.

There were rumours circulating online that changing your location settings with either console might result in a ban, but social media has been flooded with success stories.

items.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ is the best-reviewed game of 2026: “A masterpiece”

Grand Theft Auto 6 has become the best-reviewed game of 2026 ahead of its launch tomorrow (Thursday November 19).

Grand Theft Auto 6 isn’t out yet but it’s already broken plenty of records. It’s reportedly the most expensive video game ever made and has broken pre-order records on both PlayStation and Xbox consoles.

The review embargo for the long-awaited sequel to Grand Theft Auto 5 lifted earlier today (Wednesday November 18) and, according to aggregate site Metacritic , it’s comfortably the best-reviewed game of 2026. Based on 115 reviews, Grand Theft Auto 6 has a near-perfect Metacritic score of 99 per cent.

“In Grand Theft Auto 6 , Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have yet seen. items.title: ‘Everything he said sounded like a song title!’ The rackety, romantic life of Bobby Charles, alligator-befriending bard of the bayou
items.summary:
He was nearly an early rock’n’roll star but took a different path, from Fats Domino to the Band and pro-environment songwriting. As a career-spanning box set is released, those who knew him remember an American original

‘I was listening to Bob Dylan’s Theme Time radio show,” says Korey Richey, multi-instrumentalist with LCD Soundsystem, “and he said, ‘Bobby Charles is best known as a songwriter, but he has one of the most melodious voices ever transmuted into a piece of vinyl.’ I thought about it, and I agree: Bobby Charles was something else.”

Something else, indeed. Charles (1938–2010) was unable to play an instrument yet wrote songs sung by everyone from Fats Domino to Etta James to Kris Kristofferson. Signed to Chess Records in 1955 aged 17, he was on the verge of becoming a star at the dawn of rock’n’roll, but a preference for living reclusively – with a pet alligator – ensured he vanished from sight, and his music has long been unavailable. “He was a very strange guy, a loner,” says one of his Louisiana contemporaries, 88-year-old Johnnie Allan. “He knew what he had and wouldn’t compromise.” Now a box set, The Bobby Charles Story, containing almost every recording Charles released, aims to establish the Cajun magus as one of the greats.

items.t: ‘Everything he said sounded like a song title!’ The rackety, romantic life of Bobby Charles, alligator-befriending bard of the bayou

items.title: James Blunt legally changes name to ‘Ryan Air’ after scoring Number One album
items.summary:
James Blunt has legally changed his name to ‘Ryan Air’ after promising to do so if his new album went to the top of the charts.

READ MORE: James Blunt: “Occasionally I looked at myself and thought, ‘I’d punch you in the face’” 

The singer and Celebrity Traitors star dropped his ‘Airplane Mode’ album on November 6, and told fans that he would change his name to ‘Ryan Air’ if they helped get it to Number One on the UK charts.

Now, after it went to the top of the charts and became his first UK number one in 19 years, he has followed through on his promise, and shared a photo seemingly confirming that he has changed his name.

He posted a photo on Instagram, showing that he has submitted an application to change his name. In the document, it showed that the singer – real name James Hillier Blount – had filed for his new name to be ‘Ryan Bel Air’.

In the screenshot, he also shared a caption, saying that the move “cost me £53.05.”

View this post on Instagram 

‘Airplane Mode’ is his chart topper since 2007’s ‘All The Lost Souls’, and his first album – 2005’s ‘Back To Bedlam’ – also went to the top spot and spent 10 weeks there.

This isn’t the first time that Blunt has offered to change his name if he gets to the top of the charts. Back in 2024, he promised to change his name to ‘Blunty McBluntface’ if fans could get the 20th-anniversary re-release of ‘Back To Bedlam’ to the Number One spot.

The name was chosen by fans after a poll went up online, however the album only managed to get to Number Seven though, meaning that he didn’t have to follow through on the promise.…
items.t: James Blunt legally changes name to ‘Ryan Air’ after scoring Number One album

items.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ review: one of the best games ever made
items.summary:
“T his is art,” says hyperactive truther Cal, sitting his good friend Jason Duval down to play a gothic arthouse video game – one of four fictional titles fully playable in Grand Theft Auto 6 . And the same is undoubtedly expected of GTA 6 as a whole. It’s the most anticipated game of all time, the biggest entertainment launch in history, the work of 6,000 developers over a decade that seemingly the entire world has been waiting 13 years to play. If the latest Rockstar release is anything less than Louvre-worthy, it will be considered a flop.

Read more: Every song confirmed for the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack so far 

Let’s puncture some of the wilder fantasies right now. GTA 6 is not a 13-year leap forward in gaming. At twice the size of GTA 5 , it’s enormous and rich with experiences, but in-game it doesn’t feel noticeably bigger or busier than, say, San Andreas . Its gigantic map has large rural areas you’ll only really explore post-story and, far from being able to burgle every house, you can’t even enter most restaurants on its art deco Ocean Drive. It’s long, but whichever exec took 80 hours to complete the story campaign clearly cares too much about damaging expensive cars. We screeched, scraped and pranged our way through it in 52 hours, roughly the same as Red Dead Redemption 2 . Sure, this is a beautiful game – but GTA 6 is a next-gen upgrade in line with many other current triple-A games rather than a photorealistic real-world simulation. And it still can’t do hair or water.

The expectation it does fulfil, though, is that of one of the best games ever made.…
items.t: ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ review: one of the best games ever made

items.title: ‘The Hunger Games’ prequel ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ is dividing critics: “An origin story nobody wanted” or a series highlight?
items.summary:
The Hunger Games prequel Sunrise On The Reaping is out Friday (November 20) but the film is already dividing critics.

Based on Suzanne Collins’ fifth book in The Hunger Games series, Sunrise On The Reaping takes place 24 years before the events of the first novel. It focuses on the 50th annual Hunger Games, which was won by Haymitch Abernathy who went on to mentor Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark.

Sunrise On The Reaping sees the return of original movie stars Jennifer Lawrence (Katniss), Woody Harrelson (Haymitch) and Josh Hutcherson (Peeta) while young Haymitch is played by Joseph Zada. Ralph Fiennes takes over from Donald Sutherland as President Snow with Jesse Plemons, Kieran Culkin, Glenn Close, McKenna Grace, Elle Fanning and Maya Hawkes also starring.

After strong first reactions , the prequel has received a real mixed response from critics and currently has a Rotten Tomatoes score of 75 per cent, based on 80 reviews.

“Here is yet another iteration of the utterly exhausted, unbearably extended and now surreally boring Hunger Games franchise,” wrote The Guardian ’s Peter Bradshaw in his one-star review. This film has no actual interest and no authentic reason to exist, other than to gouge an income stream out of its fanbase.”

“The longest and most expensive film in the franchise is an origin story nobody wanted about a clueless dystopian klutz played by a perfunctory Joseph Zada,” said The Times ’ Kevin Maher in his two-star review.

“ Sunrise On The Reaping is far stronger than so many fished-from-the-bin franchise revivals. The filmmaker has three other…
items.t: ‘The Hunger Games’ prequel ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ is dividing critics: “An origin story nobody wanted” or a series highlight?

items.title: They’re one of the UK’s greatest cult bands – who swore they’d never reunite. What brought Life Without Buildings back together?
items.summary:
The Scottish quartet existed for just three years at the turn of the millennium. But after Frank Ocean and TikTok thrilled to Sue Tompkins’ unique vocals, they’re back. They explain their fears about ‘spoiling the joy’

‘I’m excited, I’m scared, I’m anxious – that bubbling feeling, like when you’re on a rollercoaster, at the very top, just before the big drop.”

On a drizzly afternoon in July, huddled with her three bandmates in the cramped cupboard that’s the dressing room of Glasgow venue Mono, Sue Tompkins is managing her feelings ahead of her first proper gig with Life Without Buildings in almost a quarter of a century. “Everybody coming is invited, it’s secret, nobody paid much to get in, the profits are going to charity,” adds guitarist Robert Dallas Gray, sat beside her, as much to steady his own nerves as to explain the circumstances of tonight’s show. “I hope people aren’t looking at it like we’re fucking entertainers.”

items.t: They’re one of the UK’s greatest cult bands – who swore they’d never reunite. What brought Life Without Buildings back together?

items.title: ‘Mick Jagger should fold up his penis and go home’: the caustic genius of music critic Robert Christgau
items.summary:
Beloved for his savage takedowns and rhapsodic raves, the legendary Village Voice reviewer opens up in a candid new documentary

Rows and rows of CDs, albums, cassettes and books creak and groan on shelves that snake around the walls and choke the halls of an apartment in New York City’s East Village. The clutter that sprawls through its rooms is so dense it suggests the twistiest parts of a Moroccan medina or a warren no self-respecting rabbit would allow. Buried amid the muddle is a man hunched over a computer keyboard, clacking out words meant to make sense of all the sounds that these physical media hold.

Welcome to the lair of Robert Christgau, the self-declared “Dean of American Rock Critics”, as seen in a new documentary provocatively titled The Last Critic. “Bob is someone who has probably listened to more music, and published more words about music, than anyone to walk the face of the earth, and he’s still doing it in his mid-80s,” says Matty Wishnow, who directed the film. “It’s a career that’s both unprecedented and unrepeatable.”

Continue reading...

items.title: ‘I have to sell my bum on OnlyFans to go on tour’: Kate Nash on fame, feminism and fighting the music business
items.summary:
She threw a (metaphorical) brick through Spotify’s window and exposed industry failings with her ‘Butts for Tour Buses’ campaign. Now the singer is embracing her Irish roots with her new album’s fighting spirit

Kate Nash was standing on a fire truck in a showgirl outfit complete with white tights and pink G-string, shouting through a loudhailer about the music industry’s failure to pay artists fairly, when she wondered if she’d gone too far. It was 2024 and the truck, which made pit stops outside the London offices of Spotify and Live Nation, had a large black-and-white picture of Nash’s bum on the back along with the words “Butts for Tour Buses” – a reference to her newly launched OnlyFans account, which she was using to fund her tour.

That afternoon, she called her manager Kat. “I told her: ‘I’ve thrown a brick through the window at Spotify.’ She went: ‘What, literally?’ and I said: ‘No, but I’ve been standing outside their offices with a megaphone, so that relationship is over. I don’t think we’ll be making their New Music Friday feature.’ And we didn’t.” [see footnote]

items.t: ‘I have to sell my bum on OnlyFans to go on tour’: Kate Nash on fame, feminism and fighting the music business

items.title: Ocean Colour Scene review – no other band of their era can do it like this
items.summary:
Ulster Hall, Belfast
With two sets of fathers and sons now in the group, as they play all of Moseley Shoals on its 30th anniversary, the indie stalwarts have aged into seismic and soulful performers

‘It’s only 30 years ago,” Simon Fowler says of Moseley Shoals. He would seem to mean it, but 30 years makes Ocean Colour Scene’s breakthrough album as old now as Revolver was when they were making it. The band once derided for raiding the 60s are now heritage themselves. They open the album’s anniversary tour on the stage where Led Zeppelin first played Stairway to Heaven, and you can’t help but appreciate the lineage.

They walk on to Green Onions, fresh from the Crown Bar, and open with You’ve Got It Bad, all supreme Motown stomp. Fowler sings with a hand in his pocket and looks taken aback by the welcome. The casualness is a conduit: his voice has aged into something close to peak Joe Cocker, grained at the edges, honey underneath. Lining Your Pockets is more resounding than ever.

Continue reading...
items.t: Ocean Colour Scene review – no other band of their era can do it like this

items.title: Paris Paloma review – arena-scale alt-pop drama from a singer on her way to bigger things
items.summary:
Bristol Beacon
The UK artist combines feminist fury with accessible melodies and a dramatic flair that sees her alternately pogoing and seeking out the wind machines at the prow of the stage

People are dancing to a song they don’t know, with flower garlands in their hair and their arms around their friends. This reaction to Fairy Dance, an unreleased track written about the community that has sprung up around her music, says a lot about the moment Paris Paloma finds herself in, and tonight’s show feels for all the world like a stepping stone to bigger things.

Throughout, Paloma leans in to the built-in drama of songs from her second album, The Fatal Flaw, which pairs ornate folk arrangements with the sort of arena-sized alt-pop production favoured by Florence + the Machine. With a sculpture inspired by surrealist Ithell Colquhoun’s Tree of Veins dominating the stage, she falls to her knees to deliver high notes and seeks out wind machines at the prow of the stage, her flowing crimson dress buffeted as if on a wintry moor.

items.t: Paris Paloma review – arena-scale alt-pop drama from a singer on her way to bigger things
